title: Login Survives Even When Android Kills the App | vitalii.no
description:
Google blocks sign-in inside embedded WebViews, so the app sends the user to Chrome for login and waits for Chrome to hand control back. The catch: Android is free to kill the app's background process while Chrome is still open, and when that happens the hand-back has nowhere to land — the login finishes in Chrome, but the app never finds out, leaving the user stuck on the login screen with no idea why.

Before sending the user to Chrome, the app now generates a random nonce and attaches it to the redirect URL. Once Chrome finishes the Google OAuth flow, it hands that nonce to the server, and the app — whether or not it's still the same process — polls the server every 2 seconds until the login is confirmed. A conflicting intent filter that let Chrome's own auth page reopen inside the app and intercept the token was removed, and a completed sign-in now takes priority over Android's restored page state on restart.

A Google sign-in started in Chrome now reaches the app even if Android killed its process mid-flow — the polling loop checks in every 2 seconds instead of depending on a one-shot hand-back that could silently fail.
